title: 35-30 Us, Because I Said So
seoTitle: Commanders vs. Bengals Prediction: Joe Burrow vs. Our Defense, Bill Vinovich and a 35-30 Call
summary: Bengals at Commanders on Monday night: Joe Burrow and the best receiver duo in football against a defense that's finally figuring it out, Bill Vinovich's crew, the week's best press-conference lines, and a 35-30 pick for the only reason I've got.
wireTaps: 35-30 us. One of you said 42-28 Bengals. Tell me why I'm wrong.
paragraphs: It's early Sunday morning and I'm awake for no reason, because I'm old now. So I checked the picks. Four of you have us winning a shootout. Then, sometime overnight, one bold soul walked in and called it Bengals 42, Commanders 28. I respect the honesty. I would never do it, but I respect it.
My pick is Commanders 35, Bengals 30. I never pick against us, for better or worse. Usually worse.
Links up top, like always: [who's reffing Monday](whos-reffing.html), and [Call Your Shot](leaderboard.html), where you can pick the score before kickoff. Picks lock at 8:15 Monday.
## Burrow vs. Our Defense

Let's be honest about what's walking into Northwest Stadium on Monday. This is one of those games we absolutely should lose. The Bengals have scored 31 or more five weeks in a row, and they have the best receiver duo in the NFL coming right down our face. Tee Higgins is good. Ja'Marr Chase is insane, before the catch and after it. Quinn spent a good chunk of his Thursday presser talking about Chase breaking tackles, which is coach for "please, somebody wrap him up."

And yet. Our defense is actually coming together. We gave up 24 or more in each of the first five games. We haven't given up 24 in the four since. Quinn credits the takeaways, better tackling, and Daronte Jones cutting a layer or two out of a scheme that wasn't clicking. Even the team podcast admits there's no real way to shut down Chase and Higgins, so the plan is to keep Burrow in the pocket and take away the second-reaction stuff, where he turns a broken play into a backyard game. London Fletcher wants the pressure coming up the middle. So do I, loudly, from the couch.

Here's the part I didn't see coming: their defense is sneaky good too. It gets after the quarterback. Five weeks into the season they were tied for third in the league in sacks and fourth in "havoc," which is a real stat and also how I'd describe my Sundays. Jayden said it himself on Thursday: they fly to the ball and they take it away.

And they have two guys who know us way too well. Jonathan Allen, eight seasons here and two Pro Bowls, comes home with the other team and called it an "emotional" return. I'll be emotional too, Jonathan, mostly about our guards. And Dexter Lawrence, who spent years being a menace to us twice a year in New York, is now a menace in orange.

The good news is you can run on them. They're in the bottom half of the league against the run and 30th on third down. Which is why I need Jacory Croskey-Merritt healthy so badly it's embarrassing. His practice window is open, and Quinn is "definitely not ruling out" Monday.

Then there's our offensive line. Laremy Tunsil is on IR after triceps surgery, so it's Sam Cosmi, who is a real NFL guard, Josh Conerly Jr., who gets a pass, and three guys I'd describe, lovingly, as somebody else's backups. With Allen and Lawrence coming up the middle. Cool. Cool cool cool.
## Ref Watch: Bill Vinovich

Quick one, because the Hail Mail got the long version. Bill Vinovich has the game. His crews throw 13.2 flags a game, right at the league average. He's had us twice, and both times we drew more flags than the other team. That's not him. That's us. Every game he's worked is on the [Ref Watch page](whos-reffing.html).
## What They Said This Week
The Breakdowns were good this week. Here's what stuck.

Our backup quarterback is the Bachelor. Sam Hartman is the next Bachelor. This is real. Quinn said he's thrilled for him and has zero advice. Jayden said he gets no say in the judging, that's all Sam. I have so many questions and I'm afraid of every answer.

Braveheart. Quinn said the big third-down stand against the Giants "felt like it was Braveheart" at the line of scrimmage. Then somebody asked Deatrich Wise Jr. how he knew the Giants' sneak came up short, and he said, "Cuz I stopped him." Chris said the exact same thing in the group chat while it was happening: "Bad spot. We stopped him." Chris and Deatrich Wise Jr. are the same person now. I don't make the rules.
The SS Impala. On the team podcast, Fred Smoot nicknamed Sonny Styles the "SS Impala," because he'll run you down. It's perfect, and I'm never calling him anything else.
A beer spear. There's a new limited-edition beer spear at the stadium that holds more than a pint. I don't know who asked for this. It was me. I asked for this.
Jayden downloaded GTA 6 and hasn't played it yet. That's the most impressive thing anyone said all week.
## The Group Chat

Jason, the morning after the Giants game, with the most honest scouting report of the season: "We still stink, the Giants stink, Dallas stinks. Each team has one thing better than the others, but ours is the QB which is the most important." He also said that at some point we have to beat a team we shouldn't. Jason, this is that team.

And me, that same morning: "preseason i would have said cincy was a win but man they look unstoppable on offense right now." Past me was an idiot. Present me is also an idiot, but at least I'm consistent.
## Meanwhile, in Charlottesville

Quick detour. UVA beat North Carolina 41-24 yesterday to get bowl eligible, and Tony Elliott is now 2-0 against Bill Belichick. Two and oh. Against the guy with six Super Bowls. If Tony Elliott can do that, Dan Quinn can beat Joe Burrow once. That's the logic I'm working with.
## The Pick

So here's where I land. I think Burrow puts on a clinic. I think Chase does something Monday night that ends up on every highlight show for a week. But I've seen weirder stuff happen, and somehow, someway, we pull this out. Why? Because I said so.
Commanders 35, Bengals 30.
Monday, 8:15 on ESPN. All black. Hail.
